name: Amorepacific Museum of Art (APMA)
summary: Free museum inside David Chipperfield's monolithic white Amorepacific HQ tower in Yongsan.
description: APMA occupies the ground and basement floors of Amorepacific's headquarters, a huge white aluminum-fin monolith with a garden carved through its base. Exhibitions rotate through blue-chip Korean and international artists in a calm, minimal, museum-grade space, and admission is always free. The building also holds apLAP, a two-story public library-lounge, and AMORE YONGSAN, a beauty concept floor. From 1 Sep 2026 the museum shows "Sol LeWitt: Open Structure" through Feb 2027, so it's running during the whole trip window.
highlights: David Chipperfield's white monolith facade and sunken garden
Sol LeWitt: Open Structure exhibition (Sep 2026–Feb 2027)
apLAP two-story public library lounge
AMORE YONGSAN beauty concept floor downstairs
tips: Closed Mondays and on New Year's Day, Seollal and Chuseok — plan for 27 or 29 Sep instead of the holiday itself.
Free, no ticket needed for most shows; just walk in via the ground-floor entrance.
Combine with a walk along the Han River at Yongsan Family Park, a few minutes away.
The apLAP library floor is a quiet, air-conditioned place to rest even if the art isn't your thing.

reviews.text: Amorepacific Museum of Art offers completely free admission to all exhibitions, unusual among Seoul's major art museums.
The building itself — a huge white monolith by David Chipperfield — is as much the attraction as whatever's on the walls inside.

hours.note: Closed Mondays, New Year's Day, Seollal and Chuseok holidays.

chuseok.note: Closed 24–26 Sep for the Chuseok holiday (museum policy explicitly closes for Seollal and Chuseok); reopens 27 Sep, then closed again 28 Sep for its regular Monday closure.

name: SongEun Art Space
summary: Herzog & de Meuron's perforated-concrete tower in Cheongdam, a free non-profit contemporary art space.
description: SongEun is a private, non-profit foundation housed in a striking nine-story building by Pritzker winners Herzog & de Meuron — a solid concrete volume wrapped in a diagonal lattice of tiny perforations that glows at night. Inside, polished white galleries host rotating contemporary art shows and an annual emerging-artist prize exhibition, all free. It's one of the best pieces of new architecture in Cheongdam and rarely crowded with tourists.
highlights: Herzog & de Meuron's perforated-concrete facade, lit up after dark
Free rotating contemporary art exhibitions
SongEun Art Award show for emerging Korean artists
Quiet, gallery-white interior — a break from Cheongdam's shopping crowds
tips: Open weekdays only (Mon–Fri 11:00–18:30, last entry 18:10) — closed Saturday and Sunday.
General admission and docent tours need a reservation via songeun.or.kr.
It's "closed between exhibitions," so check the website's current show before making a special trip.
Pair with Boon the Shop and Dosan Park, both a short walk away.

reviews.text: In keeping with our mission to make contemporary art accessible to wide audiences, SONGEUN offers free admission to all visitors.
One of Seoul's most photogenic pieces of new architecture — a solid concrete tower perforated with thousands of tiny windows.

hours.note: Closed Saturday, Sunday, and between exhibitions.

chuseok.note: No 2026 Chuseok notice found. Regular hours are weekdays only, so 26–27 Sep (Sat/Sun) are closed anyway; 24–25 Sep are inferred closed for the Chuseok holiday since it's a small private foundation — call ahead to confirm before 28–29 Sep.

name: Genesis Studio Hanam
summary: Genesis's flagship showroom inside Starfield Hanam, with concept cars, curated tours and racing simulators.
description: The world's first standalone Genesis Studio sits on the 2nd floor of Starfield Hanam mall, a sleek, gallery-like showroom where a personal curator walks you through the current lineup and design story. Reservation-based test drives and simulator games make it more than a car dealership — it feels like a design museum for Genesis's EVs and luxury sedans. During the 2026 trip window it's hosting the Genesis Magma Racing Live Festival (24–27 Sep), showing the GMR-001 Le Mans hypercar and Magma GT3 Concept with racing simulators and a live WEC screening.
highlights: Genesis Magma Racing Live Festival, 24–27 Sep 2026: GMR-001 Le Mans hypercar & Magma GT3 Concept on display
Personal curator walkthroughs of the current Genesis lineup
Racing simulators and reaction-speed games
Reservation-based test drives (21+, valid license)
tips: Normally closed the first Monday of each month, New Year's Day, Seollal, Chuseok and the day after — but the 2026 Magma festival keeps it running through the Chuseok weekend itself.
Book the personal curating session ahead online; arriving more than 15 minutes late cancels the slot.
It's inside Starfield Hanam, so pair with Hyundai Motorstudio Hanam one floor down and the mall's food court.
No direct subway — take a taxi or the Starfield shuttle bus from Godeok Station (Line 5).

reviews.text: Genesis showcased the Magma GT3 Concept at Starfield Hanam, reflecting its intent to compete in GT3 endurance racing.
The personal curating program takes about an hour from the reservation time, with a Genesis curator explaining the vehicle and space in detail.

price.note: Free to browse; test drives free with reservation and valid license

hours.note: Follows Starfield Hanam mall hours; curating/test-drive sessions run on their own reserved schedule. Normally closed first Monday of the month, New Year's, Seollal, Chuseok + the following day.

chuseok.note: The Genesis Magma Racing Live Festival runs exactly 24–27 Sep 2026 at Starfield Hanam / Genesis Studio Hanam, so it's open through Chuseok this year despite the studio's normal policy of closing for Chuseok and the following day (28 Sep is closed under that regular policy).

name: Hyundai Motorstudio Hanam
summary: Hyundai's huge 1F flagship inside Starfield Hanam — full model lineup, cinema, cafe and test-drive zone.
description: Distinct from the smaller Gangnam Motorstudio, this is Hyundai's flagship experience space on the ground floor of Starfield Hanam, built around a full walk-through of Hyundai's current and future line-up, an EV charging and tech zone, a cinema screening brand films, and a stylish in-house cafe/restaurant. It's designed as a free, low-effort family outing — no pressure to buy, just browse futuristic concept cars and interactive displays. It keeps mall-style hours year-round, including public holidays.
highlights: Walk-through of Hyundai's current EV and ICE line-up
Interactive tech and design zones
In-house cinema and cafe/restaurant
Reservation-based test drives on-site
tips: Open 10:00–22:00 every day of the year, including Chuseok — a reliable rainy-day option when smaller museums are shut.
Combine with Genesis Studio Hanam one floor up and the rest of Starfield Hanam's food court.
No nearby subway — go by taxi/car or the mall's free shuttle bus from Godeok or Cheonho stations (Line 5/8).
Free EV charging and rest areas make it an easy stop to break up a Hanam-side day trip.

reviews.text: Hyundai Motorstudio Hanam operates year-round with a full walkthrough of the current model lineup inside Starfield Hanam.
A slick, air-conditioned way to spend an hour browsing concept cars with kids without spending a won.

chuseok.note: Published hours are 10:00–22:00 every day of the year with no holiday closure listed.

bestTime: Any time — open daily incl. holidays

name: Tamburins Seongsu
summary: Gentle Monster's fragrance-and-skincare label in a raw-concrete Seongsu flagship that feels like an art installation.
description: Tamburins' flagship fills a converted building in Seongsu's Yeonmujang-gil with brutalist raw concrete, dramatic lighting and rotating art installations — past versions have included a hanging botanical garden and sculptural scent bars. It's less a shop than a walkable art piece, and browsing is free even if you don't buy the hand creams and perfumes. Expect a line of photographers at the entrance any afternoon.
highlights: Raw-concrete brutalist interior with rotating art installations
Try-before-you-buy fragrance and hand cream bar
Frequently changing seasonal displays (check Instagram before visiting)
A five-minute walk from Ader Error Space and other Seongsu flagships
tips: Open daily 11:00–21:00, no reservation needed for the shop floor.
Best photographed on a weekday morning before the afternoon crowd arrives.
Combine with Ader Error Space, D Museum and Blue Bottle Seongsu — all within a 10-minute walk.
Nearest exit is Seongsu Station (Line 2) Exit 4, about 10 minutes on foot through Yeonmujang-gil.

reviews.text: The store carries a distinctive minimalist concrete architecture that feels more like a gallery than a beauty shop.
One of Seongsu's must-visit flagships thanks to its ever-changing installation art and iconic concrete architecture.

chuseok.note: No 2026 Chuseok closure notice found; Seongsu concept-retail flagships typically stay open through the holiday. Not independently confirmed for 2026 — worth a quick Instagram check before going.

name: Apple Myeongdong
summary: Apple's glass-fronted Myeongdong flagship with pocket gardens, a glass staircase and Asia's first Apple Pickup counter.
description: Apple's largest Korean store spans two levels at the base of a Myeongdong tower behind a full-width, double-height glass facade — the first of its kind for Apple. Pocket gardens with commissioned sculptures by Korean artists flank the entrance, a glass-and-steel staircase connects the floors, and the upper Forum level has a big video wall and city views. It's a genuinely relaxing, air-conditioned, low-effort browse in the middle of Myeongdong's shopping chaos, and every product can be tried hands-on.
highlights: Full-width double-height glass storefront with pocket gardens
Glass-riser staircase and Forum space with video wall
Every current Apple product available to try
Asia's first dedicated Apple Pickup counter
tips: Open daily 11:00–22:00, including holidays — a reliable air-conditioned break during Myeongdong shopping.
Tax refund desks are elsewhere in Myeongdong; ask staff for the nearest kiosk if buying electronics.
The upper Forum level has free seating and Han River/city views — worth the trip up even without buying anything.
Myeongdong Station (Line 4) Exit 6 is a 3-minute walk.

reviews.text: The store's horizontally supported double-height glass facade is the first installation of its kind for Apple.
Landscaped pocket gardens with commissioned sculptures by Korean artists Jaehyo Lee and VAKKI flank the storefront.

chuseok.note: No 2026 holiday notice found, but Apple's Korean flagship stores are well known to keep normal hours through Chuseok in past years. Not independently confirmed for 2026.

name: Common Ground
summary: The world's largest pop-up mall stacked from 200 cobalt-blue shipping containers near Konkuk University.
description: Common Ground is built from roughly 200 recycled shipping containers stacked into a striking cobalt-blue complex housing streetwear boutiques, an indoor Market Hall, food stalls and a weekend events space. It's an easy, low-effort browse — flat, mostly covered, air-conditioned in the container corridors — with the industrial architecture itself as photogenic as anything inside. Weekend evenings bring flea markets and live events to the central Market Ground plaza.
highlights: 200 stacked shipping containers, Instagram-famous from every angle
Street Market and Market Hall indoor boutiques
Weekend flea markets and events in the central Market Ground plaza
Casual food court with Seoul's trendy F&B brands
tips: Open 11:00–22:00 daily; some 3F restaurants stay open till 1am on weekends.
Konkuk University Station (Lines 2 & 7) Exit 3 is a 3-minute walk.
Best photographed at dusk when the container walls catch the last light.
Combine with a walk around Konkuk University's lakeside campus next door.

reviews.text: Common Ground is the world's largest container shopping mall, built by stacking around 200 repurposed shipping containers.
A young, casual, Instagram-friendly cultural platform mixing streetwear boutiques, food and weekend pop-up markets.

hours.note: Select 3F dining venues stay open until 1am Friday and Saturday.

chuseok.note: No 2026 Chuseok closure notice found; casual retail/F&B malls of this type typically stay open through the holiday. Not independently confirmed for 2026.

name: COEX K-Pop Square (WAVE)
summary: A giant curved LED screen outside COEX that makes 3D ocean waves appear to crash through the building.
description: One of Korea's largest outdoor LED screens (80m wide, 20m tall) wraps the corner of the COEX/K-pop Square building in Samseong-dong, running d'strict's anamorphic "WAVE" illusion on a loop alongside K-pop content and public art. At night the crashing-wave effect looks genuinely three-dimensional from the plaza below — it's free, always on, and needs zero effort beyond standing in the right spot with a phone camera.
highlights: d'strict's anamorphic "WAVE" 3D illusion, running continuously
80.1m x 20.1m LED screen, one of Korea's largest
Rotating K-pop and public digital art content
Right next to Starfield COEX Mall and Bongeunsa Temple
tips: It's an outdoor plaza, open 24 hours — but the wave effect reads best after dark.
Best viewing spot is the plaza directly across from the screen, not right underneath it.
Bongeunsa Station (Line 9) Exit 7 comes out almost right beside it.
Combine with Starfield COEX Mall, Starfield Library and Bongeunsa Temple, all within a few minutes' walk.

reviews.text: The WAVE creates an amazing effect as if waves are penetrating through the screen, establishing K-Pop Square as Seoul's most influential digital media landmark.
One of the largest outdoor, high-definition LED screens in South Korea, built to feature K-pop content on a giant scale.

hours.note: Outdoor public plaza and screen, always accessible; best viewed after dark.

chuseok.note: A permanent outdoor media facade with no opening hours or closures — it runs every day including Chuseok.

name: D Museum
summary: A sleek Seoul Forest photography/experiential-art museum with a rotating, made-for-Instagram exhibition.
description: Run by the Daelim Cultural Foundation, D Museum relocated to a striking modern building beside Seoul Forest in 2021, and every exhibition is built as an immersive, photogenic experience rather than a traditional gallery hang — often blending photography, design and installation art. The rooftop area doubles as a relaxed photo spot with skyline views. It's an easy, air-conditioned couple of hours that reliably impresses parents and adult kids alike.
highlights: A single large rotating exhibition designed as an immersive walk-through
Rooftop terrace with photo-friendly Seongsu skyline views
Museum shop with design-forward exhibition merchandise
A 10-minute walk from Seoul Forest park
tips: Closed Mondays, plus Lunar New Year and Chuseok — plan for 27 or 29 Sep, not the holiday itself.
Buy tickets online in advance for popular exhibitions to skip the queue.
Combine with Seoul Forest park and the Seongsu Yeonmujang-gil flagship stores nearby.
The rooftop is worth the walk up even if you find the main exhibition hit-or-miss.

tripadvisor.rank: #195 of 1,622 things to do in Seoul

reviews.text: The museum was really great and I wish I had more time to look around without having to wait on the crowds of people.
It's worth coming here — the quality of the exhibition is good, though it depends how much you're into art or design.
A waste of time and money for some, but the rooftop has a nice area for photo-taking regardless of the exhibition.

hours.note: Closed Mondays, Lunar New Year's Day and Chuseok.

chuseok.note: D Museum is closed on Mondays, Lunar New Year's Day, and Chuseok. The 2026 Chuseok holiday runs 24–26 Sep, so it reopens 27 Sep, then closes again 28 Sep for its regular Monday closure.

name: ADER Error Space Seongsu
summary: ADER Error's reimagined Seongsu flagship, its "FUTOURIST" interior turned into undulating, warped rooms.
description: For its 10th anniversary, Korean streetwear label ADER Error rebuilt its Seongsu flagship around a "FUTOURIST: Imagination builds a new world" concept — deliberately warped, undulating walls and ceilings that make the whole store feel like a glitch in reality. The ground floor sells clothing and accessories, the second floor is a cafe, and every corner is designed for photos. Because the space is large and popular, an on-site reservation is recommended to get in comfortably.
highlights: "FUTOURIST" undulating, warped architecture throughout
Ground-floor flagship store, 2nd-floor cafe
Rotating art and product installations
A five-minute walk from Tamburins Seongsu and D Museum
tips: Open 11:30–19:00; the brand recommends an on-site reservation given how popular and large the space is.
Go on a weekday to actually see the architecture without a crowd in every shot.
Combine with Tamburins, D Museum and Seoul Forest for a Seongsu design-district afternoon.
Seongsu Station (Line 2) Exit 3/4 is about a 12-minute walk through Yeonmujang-gil.

reviews.text: ADERERROR renovated its flagship Seongsu space with the theme 'FUTOURIST: Imagination builds a new world' through undulating interiors.
The flagship store covers a very large area, so an appointment is recommended before visiting.

hours.note: On-site reservation recommended due to space and popularity.

chuseok.note: No 2026 Chuseok closure notice found; treated as open like other Seongsu concept-retail flagships. Not independently confirmed — check the brand's Instagram before Chuseok.

name: Boon the Shop Cheongdam
summary: Korea's first luxury multi-brand store, rebuilt by Peter Marino into two white-marble volumes in Cheongdam.
description: Opened in 2004 as Korea's first luxury multi-brand boutique, Boon the Shop's Cheongdam flagship was rebuilt in 2014 by American architect Peter Marino into two sharp-angled white marble buildings — Building N and Building S — linked by a passageway, spread over seven floors and 55,000 sq ft. Even without buying anything, it's worth a walk-through for the architecture and rotating in-store art, and it anchors an easy stroll through Cheongdam's other design-forward flagships.
highlights: Peter Marino's two-volume white marble architecture (Building N & S)
Curated multi-brand luxury fashion across seven floors
Rotating art installations inside the store
Steps from SongEun Art Space and other Cheongdam flagships
tips: Open daily 11:00–20:00.
Even non-shoppers can walk through for the architecture — staff are used to browsers.
Combine with SongEun Art Space and the Dosan Park flagship strip for a Cheongdam design walk.
Apgujeong Rodeo Station (Suin-Bundang Line) Exit 2 is about an 8-minute walk.

reviews.text: The flagship, upgraded and reorganized by architect Peter Marino in 2014, comprises 55,000 sq ft over seven floors in two polished white marble volumes.
Boon the Shop opened in 2004 as Korea's first luxury multi-brand store.

price.note: Free to browse; luxury goods priced individually

chuseok.note: No 2026 notice found. Inferred closed on Chuseok day itself (25 Sep) as is common for high-end Korean boutiques, open the rest of the holiday period — unconfirmed, call ahead.

name: House of Shinsegae Cheongdam
summary: Shinsegae's reinvented Cheongdam gourmet hall — gray metallic shelving, dry-aged fish tech, a wellness-first edit.
description: Reopened 13 December 2025, this is the former SSG Food Market Cheongdam/Dogok completely reworked into "House of Shinsegae" — gray metallic shelving instead of Baroque fixtures, energetic music instead of classical, and a curated 6,000-item edit (down from 20,000) built around health-oriented picks rather than pure luxury. It's the first domestic store to use fish dry-aging technology with a visible aging display, and the basement holds a smoothie bar and lounge seating. It's essentially a design-forward, very clean grocery hall that doubles as a browse-and-snack stop.
highlights: Domestic-first fish dry-aging display technology
Gray-metallic, fashion-brand-style shelving and casual staff uniforms
"Twelve" premium food hall and "Twelve Wonder Bar" smoothie counter in the basement
Curated ~6,000-item wellness-focused edit aimed at Cheongdam/Apgujeong locals in their 30s–40s
tips: Reopened only in Dec 2025 — hours weren't independently confirmed for this guide; expect roughly 10:30–20:00 like sister branches and check before going.
Go for the free-to-browse food-hall atmosphere even without buying — the dry-aging fish display alone is worth seeing.
Pair with Boon the Shop and SongEun Art Space, both a short walk away in Cheongdam.
Department-store-linked branches like this typically close one day around Chuseok — call ahead for 24–26 Sep.

reviews.text: The venue departs from traditional luxury food hall aesthetics — gray metallic shelving replaces Baroque-style fixtures, and staff wear casual clothing instead of formal uniforms.
The store's first domestic application of fish dry-aging technology visualizes the aging process for shoppers.

price.note: Free to browse; groceries and prepared food priced individually

hours.note: Hours not independently confirmed since the Dec 2025 reopening — likely similar to sister branches (~10:30–20:00). Call ahead.

chuseok.note: No 2026 Chuseok notice found for this newly reopened store. Department-store-affiliated branches typically close one day around Chuseok — treat 24–26 Sep as uncertain and call ahead.
